primary jurisdiction or land effect: Federal nonintercourse rule; federal regulation of trade and land transactions with tribes.
where it applied: Indian country and dealings with tribes nationwide, as defined by the successive acts.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: State authority constrained where federal Indian-country law applied.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribal authority generally persisted except as Congress altered it.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Established/confirmed federal role in Indian affairs and Indian-country governance.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Protected treaty/tribal land from unauthorized purchase or conveyance; applicability depended on treaty/recognized tribal lands.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Authorized negotiated removal/exchange of lands; reshaped territorial geography rather than a general criminal-jurisdiction code.
where it applied: Primarily tribes east of the Mississippi targeted for exchange/removal to western territory.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: States gained practical/geographic reach as Indigenous nations were removed, but legal effects varied by treaty and litigation.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribal political communities were relocated; tribal authority continued in new treaty/reservation settings.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal executive controlled treaty negotiation/removal process.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Extinguished/exchanged many eastern treaty-recognized land interests and created western treaty/reservation geographies.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Defined “Indian country” for the Act and extended federal criminal/Indian-affairs regulation.
where it applied: Designated Indian country west of the Mississippi and other covered areas under the statute.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: Generally excluded ordinary state criminal reach in covered Indian country, subject to statutory limits.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribal internal criminal authority remained important, especially Indian-on-Indian offenses.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Precursor to the General Crimes Act framework for federal offenses in Indian country.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Supplied a federal statutory geography separate from particular treaty lines.

measure: Indian Appropriations Act (end of treaty making)
primary jurisdiction or land effect: Ended recognition of tribes as independent nations for future treaty-making; preserved existing treaties.
where it applied: Nationwide, for future relations with federally recognized tribes.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: No direct general transfer of state criminal jurisdiction.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Existing tribal/treaty rights were not abrogated solely by this provision.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Congressional/statutory governance increasingly displaced new treaties.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Existing treaty boundaries/obligations remained; no new treaties thereafter.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Created federal jurisdiction over enumerated major offenses by Indians in Indian country.
where it applied: Indian country nationwide; applies based on offender, offense, and location.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: States generally excluded absent congressional authorization.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribal authority continued but federal authority entered major-crime cases; exact concurrency doctrine is case-specific.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal courts gained jurisdiction over enumerated offenses.
treaty-boundary / land implication: No boundary alteration; operates within Indian country, including reservations/allotments as legally defined.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Authorized division of communal reservation land into individual allotments; “surplus” land could pass from tribal control.
where it applied: Reservations selected for allotment, subject to statutory and treaty-specific exceptions.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: Checkerboarding later complicated state reach; no blanket state criminal grant.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Diminished territorial land base and practical governance, but did not itself abolish tribal criminal jurisdiction.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal trust and allotment administration expanded.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Fragmented reservation land; individual trust allotments remained legally significant Indian-country land.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Extended allotment/assimilation program in Indian Territory; curtailed Five Tribes’ governmental institutions.
where it applied: Indian Territory / Five Civilized Tribes (present-day Oklahoma).
state criminal jurisdiction implication: Changed territorial governance in Indian Territory; precise criminal jurisdiction depended on later federal/Oklahoma law.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Dismantled or constrained Five Tribes’ formal governmental institutions.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal control over allotment and governance in Indian Territory increased.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Allotted tribal land and prepared “surplus” dispositions in Indian Territory.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Authorized early fee patents for allottees deemed competent; subjected recipients to state/county civil and criminal laws.
where it applied: Allotted Indians/reservation allotments nationwide where the act applied.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: State civil/criminal jurisdiction attached to allottees receiving fee patents under the statute.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Trust-status loss narrowed land-based protections; tribal power questions remained fact/law dependent.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal Secretary determined competency and patent timing.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Accelerated conversion of some trust allotments to fee land, deepening checkerboarding.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Expanded federal administrative control over inheritance, partition, and restrictions affecting allotted land.
where it applied: Individual Indian allotments nationwide within statutory scope.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: No blanket state criminal grant; fee/trust status affected jurisdictional analysis.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribal land base remained fragmented.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Secretary/BIA authority over restricted allotments and heirship expanded.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Affected whether allotments stayed restricted/trust or entered fee ownership.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Conferred U.S. citizenship while preserving property rights; altered citizenship/status, not a broad criminal-jurisdiction transfer.
where it applied: All noncitizen Indians born in the United States.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: State political membership expanded; criminal jurisdiction in Indian country still governed by federal Indian law.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Did not itself terminate tribal citizenship or inherent governmental authority.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: No general change to federal Indian-country criminal statutes.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Expressly preserved rights to tribal or other property.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Ended further allotment, extended trust protections, authorized land restoration/acquisition, and enabled tribal constitutions.
where it applied: Eligible federally recognized tribes; some tribes voted against/otherwise fell outside particular provisions.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: No general state criminal grant.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Reaffirmed/structured tribal self-government; criminal powers remained constrained by other federal law.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal trust land acquisition and supervision remained central.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Stopped new allotment and enabled restoration/acquisition of tribal land; did not erase existing checkerboarding.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Extended IRA-style organization, land acquisition, and cooperative authority to Oklahoma tribes.
where it applied: Oklahoma Indian tribes/communities within statutory eligibility.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: No blanket state criminal grant.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Supported formal tribal organization in Oklahoma.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal approval/acquisition mechanisms continued.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Supported acquisition/holding of land for Oklahoma tribes; not a restoration of every former treaty boundary.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Authorized tribal mineral leasing with federal approval, strengthening tribal role in resource-land administration.
where it applied: Tribal lands nationwide subject to the Act.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: No direct criminal-jurisdiction transfer.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribes participate in leasing decisions under federal statutory framework.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Secretary approval and federal trust role required.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Applies to tribal lands; does not redraw reservation/treaty boundaries.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Created commission to hear claims against the United States, including treaty/land claims.
where it applied: Claims by tribes, bands, and identifiable groups against the United States.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: No direct criminal-jurisdiction allocation.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Provided a federal forum for tribal claims but did not itself restore sovereign criminal authority.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal claims adjudication mechanism.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Addressed compensation/claims arising from land and treaty losses; generally did not restore land boundaries.

measure: 1948 revision/codification of federal Indian-country criminal provisions
primary jurisdiction or land effect: Codified Indian-country definition and General Crimes/Major Crimes framework.
where it applied: Indian country nationwide: reservations, dependent Indian communities, and Indian allotments with unextinguished title.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: States generally lack jurisdiction unless Congress provides otherwise.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribal jurisdiction persists subject to federal statutes and Supreme Court doctrine.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Defines federal criminal-jurisdiction geography and major-crime coverage.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Makes individual trust allotments part of statutory Indian country; treaty line alone is not the only geography.

formal citation / status: H. Con. Res. 108 (policy resolution; not a statute)
primary jurisdiction or land effect: Announced termination policy for named tribes and directed a shift toward state-law treatment.
where it applied: Named tribes/groups and a nationwide federal policy agenda.
PL-280 status: Context for enactment; not PL-280 itself.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: Policy sought state-law assimilation; no direct jurisdictional grant by the resolution alone.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Sought ending federal recognition/supervision for targeted tribes.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Sought withdrawal of federal services/supervision.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Termination policy threatened federal trust/treaty land protections; actual effects followed particular statutes.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Transferred/authorized broad state criminal jurisdiction in covered Indian country and withdrew much federal 18 USC 1152/1153 authority there.
where it applied: Mandatory: most Indian country in CA, MN, NE, OR, WI; Alaska added at statehood, with statutory exceptions. Optional assumption occurred in some other states before 1968.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: Broadly expanded state criminal jurisdiction in covered Indian country; details/exceptions are state- and reservation-specific.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Did not itself reduce or expand tribal criminal jurisdiction; overlapping practice/doctrine is complex.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal General/Major Crimes Act authority became very limited in covered PL-280 areas.
treaty-boundary / land implication: No direct boundary redraw; applies in legally defined Indian country.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Ended federal supervision/trust relationship for Menominee and subjected property/governance to state-law transition.
where it applied: Menominee Tribe and its Wisconsin reservation lands.
PL-280 status: Wisconsin was a mandatory PL-280 state; termination produced additional state-law effects.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: State jurisdiction and law became central after termination, subject to later restoration.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Federal recognition/governmental protections were ended until restoration legislation.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal trust supervision ended during termination.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Reservation/trust status was dismantled during termination; later restored by 1973 legislation.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Terminated federal supervision and provided for disposition of Klamath property.
where it applied: Klamath Tribe and covered property in Oregon.
PL-280 status: Oregon was a mandatory PL-280 state.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: State authority expanded in the termination setting, subject to later legal developments.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Federal recognition/protections were terminated until restoration.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal trust relationship ended during termination.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Provided for disposition/transfer of Klamath property; restoration did not automatically re-create all former land status.

formal citation / status: Pub. L. 90-284, title II, 82 Stat. 77; 25 USC 1301–1304
primary jurisdiction or land effect: Applied specified rights constraints to tribal governments; authorized federal habeas review; also required tribal consent for new state PL-280 assumptions after 1968.
where it applied: Tribal governments nationwide; PL-280 consent rule applied prospectively to state assumptions.
PL-280 status: Constrained future optional assumptions by requiring tribal consent; did not automatically repeal existing PL-280.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: Prevents new state assumptions without tribal consent (and later federal statutory process).
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Imposed statutory rights requirements and federal habeas review, while recognizing powers of self-government.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal court habeas review of detention under tribal authority.
treaty-boundary / land implication: No direct boundary change.

measure: Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act
primary jurisdiction or land effect: Authorized tribes to contract/compact to administer federal programs, strengthening governmental capacity.
where it applied: Federally recognized tribes and eligible tribal organizations nationwide.
PL-280 status: No change to PL-280 allocation by itself.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: No general state criminal change.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Enhanced tribal administration/self-governance; not an independent expansion of inherent criminal jurisdiction.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal functions/funds administered through contracts/compacts; trust responsibility remained.
treaty-boundary / land implication: No direct redrawing of treaty/reservation boundaries.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Allocated child-custody jurisdiction and placement preferences to protect tribal interests.
where it applied: Indian child-custody proceedings nationwide; exclusive tribal jurisdiction in reservation cases subject to statutory exceptions.
PL-280 status: No general PL-280 repeal; special statutory rules apply.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: State courts must apply ICWA transfer, notice, intervention, and placement provisions in covered proceedings.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribal courts have exclusive or transferable jurisdiction as specified by ICWA.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal statutory standards govern state/tribal proceedings; not a general federal criminal law.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Operates by Indian child/tribal membership and reservation domicile, not treaty boundary alone.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Created federal/tribal/state framework for gaming on Indian lands; compacts govern Class III gaming.
where it applied: “Indian lands” nationwide; Class III gaming requires tribal-state compact unless another statutory route applies.
PL-280 status: PL-280 does not itself displace IGRA framework.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: States negotiate/implement compacts and may exercise agreed roles.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Tribal regulatory authority is central, subject to IGRA and compacts.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: NIGC/federal oversight and statutory enforcement roles.
treaty-boundary / land implication: Applies to Indian lands as statutorily defined, not every ancestral/treaty-cession area.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Expanded tribal sentencing authority subject to safeguards and improved federal/tribal justice coordination.
where it applied: Tribal courts and Indian-country justice systems nationwide, subject to statutory eligibility and implementation.
PL-280 status: No categorical change; PL-280-specific operation remains fact/state dependent.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: No blanket state jurisdiction change.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Permits enhanced tribal sentencing where statutory procedural requirements are met.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Strengthened federal accountability/coordination and reporting in Indian-country justice.
treaty-boundary / land implication: No direct boundary change; applies through Indian-country/tribal justice geography.

primary jurisdiction or land effect: Recognized special tribal criminal jurisdiction over covered crimes by certain non-Indians, subject to statutory conditions; 2022 expanded covered crimes.
where it applied: Indian country of participating tribes; jurisdiction is concurrent and limited by statutory conditions.
PL-280 status: Does not repeal PL-280; state/federal authority is expressly not eliminated.
state criminal jurisdiction implication: State jurisdiction, where it exists, remains concurrent/not eliminated.
tribal criminal jurisdiction implication: Participating tribes may exercise special tribal criminal jurisdiction over covered crimes as specified.
federal criminal jurisdiction implicatio: Federal jurisdiction remains concurrent/not eliminated.
treaty-boundary / land implication: No direct boundary change; confined to Indian country of participating tribes.
